subject: Future Tech
title: Space Elevators: Dream or Future?
description: A micro-lesson that makes Space Elevators: Dream or Future? usable.

hook.text: A space elevator would be a cable stretching from Earth's surface to orbit.

buildup.text: Arthur C. Clarke popularized the idea in 1979. A counterweight beyond geostationary orbit keeps the cable taut.

discovery.text: Carbon nanotubes might be strong enough for the cable, but no one can manufacture them at the required scale yet.

twist.text: A lunar space elevator is far more feasible.

climax.text: If a space elevator works, launch costs drop to dollars per kilogram, opening space to ordinary people.

punchline.text: The elevator pitch for space is literal.

quiz.question: What material might be strong enough for a space elevator cable?
